Package io.github.libxposed.api

Interface XposedInterface.Chain

Enclosing interface:
XposedInterface
public static interface XposedInterface.Chain
Interceptor chain for a method or constructor. Chain objects cannot be shared among threads or reused after XposedInterface.Hooker.intercept(Chain) ends.

    • proceedWith

      Object proceedWith(@NonNull Object thisObject) throws Throwable
      Proceeds to the next interceptor in this chain with the same arguments and the given this object. Static method interceptors should not call this method.

      This changes only the receiver used by the rest of the current chain. It does not change the executable returned by getExecutable(), select a different override, or switch to another executable's hook chain. When this chain reaches its end, the framework invokes the original implementation of getExecutable() on thisObject.

      For example, if getExecutable() is Parent.foo, calling this method with a Child object still invokes the original Parent.foo on that object. It does not dispatch to Child.foo or run hooks registered for Child.foo. Use an XposedInterface.Invoker to start a new invocation when virtual dispatch is desired.

      thisObject must be an instance of the declaring class of getExecutable().

      Parameters:
      thisObject - The this object for the call
      Returns:
      The result returned from the next interceptor, or from the original executable if the current interceptor is the last one in the chain.

      For void methods and constructors, always returns null.

      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if thisObject is not compatible with the declaring class of getExecutable()
      Throwable - if any interceptor or the original executable throws an exception

    • proceedWith

      Object proceedWith(@NonNull Object thisObject, @NonNull Object[] args) throws Throwable
      Proceeds to the next interceptor in this chain with the given arguments and this object. Static method interceptors should not call this method.

      This changes the receiver and arguments used by the rest of the current chain, but not which executable the chain belongs to. It does not select a different override or switch to another executable's hook chain. When this chain reaches its end, the framework invokes the original implementation of getExecutable() on thisObject, using args.

      For example, if getExecutable() is Parent.foo, calling this method with a Child object still invokes the original Parent.foo on that object. It does not dispatch to Child.foo or run hooks registered for Child.foo. Use an XposedInterface.Invoker to start a new invocation when virtual dispatch is desired.

      thisObject must be an instance of the declaring class of getExecutable().

      Parameters:
      thisObject - The this object for the call
      args - The arguments used for the call
      Returns:
      The result returned from the next interceptor, or from the original executable if the current interceptor is the last one in the chain.

      For void methods and constructors, always returns null.

      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if thisObject is not compatible with the declaring class of getExecutable()
      Throwable - if any interceptor or the original executable throws an exception
